bull_thesis: Technip Energies is the world's leading engineering contractor for liquefied natural gas (LNG) plants and, increasingly, for the equipment that strips carbon out of industrial processes. The bull case rests on four things that are verifiably true today. First, the order book is at a record and the demand is not in question: first-quarter 2026 order intake was €6.05 billion — more than the entire 2025 total — driven by the North Field West award in Qatar (announced 2026-02-25), Coral Norte floating LNG in Mozambique, SkyNRG's sustainable aviation fuel plant and an authorisation to advance Commonwealth LNG in the United States. Group backlog rose 27% from year-end to €20.2 billion, or 2.8 times last year's revenue, and the chief financial officer confirmed on 2026-04-30 that no contracts had been cancelled through the Middle East disruption — it was, in his words, 'just a shift' of activity into 2027 and 2028. Second, the quality of earnings is genuinely improving. The Technology, Products and Services segment — the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm — lifted its EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, as a share of revenue) from 12.9% in 2024 to a record 14.3% in 2025 and 15.3% in the first quarter of 2026, while the Ecovyst catalyst business acquired on 2025-12-31 adds over €200 million of revenue at roughly 25% margins, about 70% of it tied to customers' day-to-day operating spend rather than to one-off projects. Return on invested capital has moved from 10.5% to 11.3% and return on equity stands at 23.8%. Third, the balance sheet is genuinely strong: roughly €1 billion of net cash on management's own honest measure (excluding money customers paid in advance), which funded a €1.00 dividend paid on 2026-05-20 and a €150 million buyback, without touching the investment-grade credit rating. Fourth, this is an asset-light business with negative capital employed — customers fund the work — which is why it converts around 90% of profit into free cash. If the Strait of Hormuz reopens and the €500-600 million of deferred revenue flows back in during 2027, the 2028 framework of more than €8.6 billion of revenue and more than €800 million of EBITDA remains intact, and the shares should re-rate toward the mid-€40s. The conditions that must hold: the strait reopens within roughly two quarters; the deferred revenue returns rather than evaporates; project margins absorb the extra security and logistics cost as management expects; and the technology segment's record margin survives the loss of the ethylene-furnace deliveries that flattered 2025. Note that the peer group has already re-rated hard on a similar cycle — TechnipFMC has more than doubled off its 52-week low to $72.01 and Subsea 7 and Saipem sit near their 200-day highs — which shows what this cohort can do when the fog lifts.
bear_thesis: The bear case is not that this is a bad company. It is that the cheapness is an accounting illusion and the timing is actively bad. Start with the illusion. Three of the four things that make this stock screen cheap — price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6 times, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield, and the balance sheet's apparent €2.93 billion of net cash — are the same item counted three ways: money customers paid in advance for work not yet performed. Contract liabilities stood at €3.74 billion at year-end 2025. Management does not hide this; they publish their own honest figure, 'net cash adjusted for project-related cash of approximately EUR 1 billion.' Strip the float out and the enterprise value is roughly €4.8 billion against 2026 EBITDA of about €600 million — call it 8 times. That is a fair price for a good contractor, not a bargain, and it is why the screener's own Buffett model reads a negative 14% margin of safety while its discounted-cash-flow model reads plus 50%. The models disagree because one of them is counting the float. Worse, the float mechanically reverses: the first Qatar North Field East train reaches start-up around mid-2026, and management confirmed North Field West 'won't have a major contribution this year' — so advances stop arriving from finished projects before they arrive in scale from new ones. Now the timing. On 2026-04-30 the company cut its 2026 project-delivery revenue guidance to €5.7-6.3 billion from €6.3-6.7 billion and its margin to 6.5-7.5% from around 8%, and lowered the bottom of the technology segment's range by €100 million. First-quarter earnings per share came in at €0.48 against €0.57 expected. Critically, the chief executive's cut was explicitly conditional: 'Assuming the situation in the Middle East normalizes by the end of the second quarter, we estimate that around 500-600 million euros in revenue will be deferred beyond 2026.' That precondition has failed. The interim United States-Iran truce broke down on 2026-07-08 when Iran struck commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, and on 2026-07-12 the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy declared the strait closed — transits are running at roughly 10 per day against a pre-crisis baseline of 88. Technip Energies' largest projects sit behind that strait, in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates: 82 million tonnes per annum of LNG under construction. Half-year results land on 2026-07-30 and consensus for that print is €1.89 billion of revenue — higher than the disrupted first quarter's €1.78 billion — meaning the street is still underwriting an assumption the facts have already killed. The company also ended its buyback on 2026-07-01, removing the one price-insensitive buyer. Add the softer structural worries: project-delivery backlog fell 18% in 2025 before the first-quarter recovery; the technology segment's 2026 revenue guide of €2.0-2.2 billion is supported by only about €1 billion of backlog, with the rest resting on the acquisition, on consultancy work booked and burned, and on awards management says it has 'a clear line of sight' to; contingency levels — the number that determines whether backlog margin is real — are deliberately undisclosed, as the chief financial officer made plain when pressed in July 2025 ('maybe I won't go into the full details'); and the green-hydrogen growth leg was quietly conceded as disappointing in October 2025. What confirms the bear: a second guidance cut on 2026-07-30, or any language reclassifying the deferral from timing to loss.
consensus_delta: We disagree with the market in an unusual direction: we are more bearish than consensus on the next three months and roughly in line with it thereafter. The specific street assumption that is factually wrong is embedded in the half-year estimate for 2026-07-30: consensus sits at €1.89 billion of revenue and €0.535 of earnings per share. That revenue figure is higher than the first quarter's actual €1.78 billion and higher than the year-ago €1.83 billion — in other words, analysts are modelling a sequential recovery in a quarter during which the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted throughout. That model is inherited directly from the chief executive's own conditional language on 2026-04-30: 'Assuming the situation in the Middle East normalizes by the end of the second quarter, we estimate that around 500-600 million euros in revenue will be deferred beyond 2026.' The condition failed in public and on dated record — the truce collapsed on 2026-07-08 when Iran struck commercial ships, and the strait was declared closed on 2026-07-12 with transits at roughly 10 per day against 88 pre-crisis. The full-year consensus is equally exposed: the street's €8.06 billion revenue estimate (cut from €8.34 billion) sits almost exactly on the sum of the guidance midpoints — €6.0 billion for project delivery plus €2.05 billion for the technology segment — leaving no allowance whatsoever for a further slip. Consensus earnings per share of €2.26 (cut from €2.62) carries the same problem. The second, subtler thing the street has wrong is the balance sheet. The cheapness that draws value buyers here — a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield, 9.6 times price-to-free-cash-flow, €2.93 billion of apparent net cash — is one item counted three ways: €3.74 billion of customer advances. Management publishes the honest number, roughly €1 billion of adjusted net cash, and almost nobody uses it. On the honest number the stock is at about 8 times EBITDA, which is fair. There is no hidden value being missed; there is a hidden ordinariness being missed.
forcing_function: The catalyst is 2026-07-30 — half-year 2026 results — and it is a hard, scheduled date. It forces the issue because management gave itself no room: the 2026-04-30 guidance cut was expressly conditioned on 'the situation in the Middle East normalizes by the end of the second quarter,' and that condition demonstrably failed (truce collapse 2026-07-08, strait declared closed 2026-07-12, transits at roughly 10 per day against a pre-crisis 88). On that date the company must re-base the €500-600 million deferral estimate, mark the second-quarter revenue against a consensus of €1.89 billion that implicitly assumes a recovery that did not happen, and state whether project margins can still absorb the disruption within the 6.5-7.5% guide. Whichever way it lands, the ambiguity resolves. Secondary and softer: the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which is undated and controlled entirely by third parties, and the conversion of Commonwealth LNG's limited notice to proceed into a full notice, which management says 'will make a significant contribution to the company's backlog' but has never dated. The 2026-10 third-quarter update is the confirmation point for whether the deferral is genuinely timing. Note what is not on this list: there is no activist, no strategic process, no sum-of-the-parts breakup, no governance reset. Management is competent, aligned, and already doing the sensible things. Nobody is coming to unlock anything.
valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months and it has an unusually precise shape. The first and largest hazard is 2026-07-30, thirteen days out, when half-year results land. Management must either reaffirm guidance that was explicitly premised on the Middle East normalising by the end of the second quarter — a premise the facts destroyed on 2026-07-08 and 2026-07-12 — or cut for the second time in three months and re-base the €500-600 million deferral estimate upward. A team this careful with its numbers does not reaffirm a guide whose stated precondition has failed. Consensus of €1.89 billion of revenue for the period gives them nowhere to hide. The second hazard is mechanical and almost entirely unwatched: the customer-advance cycle turning. This balance sheet is funded by money customers pay in advance — €3.74 billion of contract liabilities at year-end. The first Qatar North Field East train reaches start-up around mid-2026, the downstream projects (Midor, Assiut, Borouge) are completing, and management confirmed that North Field West 'won't have a major contribution this year' because it is early-phase. So advances stop arriving from the projects that are finishing before they arrive in scale from the ones that are starting. That is why trailing free cash flow of €897 million sits so far above the €578 million the company actually earned in 2025 excluding one-offs, and why reported annual free cash flow already fell 24.9% year over year. Expect the free-cash-flow line and the optical net-cash figure to deteriorate toward the honest €1 billion adjusted level over the next several quarters — and expect that to read as bad news to anyone who bought the 15.5% yield. The third hazard is that the €150 million buyback ended on 2026-07-01, removing the only price-insensitive buyer in the register precisely as the news flow worsens. The fourth is margin leakage: the project-delivery margin guide has already gone from around 8% to 6.5-7.5%, and management's assurance that 'the impact on project margins should be substantially mitigated' rested on the same failed normalisation assumption. Contingency levels — the buffer that would absorb this — are deliberately undisclosed, so no outsider can check the claim. The offsetting comfort is real but slow: no contracts have been cancelled, the backlog is €20.2 billion, and the balance sheet cannot be broken by this. This is a timing wound, not a solvency one.
positioning_washout: There is no dramatic forced-selling event here, and it would be dishonest to manufacture one. This is not a yield vehicle whose shareholder base would be blown out by a distribution cut: the €1.00 dividend paid on 2026-05-20 is a roughly 3% yield on a €33 share, it was raised 18%, it is covered several times over by free cash flow, and there is no plausible scenario in which it is cut. The register is not built on income promises. What has actually changed is smaller and real. The €150 million buyback ended on 2026-07-01, which removed a daily, price-insensitive bid from the order book right as the news flow turned — the marginal buyer of the last six months has simply stopped. Beyond that, the pressure is relative rather than mechanical: this is a momentum and energy-transition holding in a cohort that has re-rated spectacularly around it, with TechnipFMC more than doubling off its low and Subsea 7 and Saipem near their 200-day highs. A second guidance cut on 2026-07-30 would push the quantitative and momentum cohort out of the one laggard in a winning group — and relative-value books have an obvious trade in funding peer longs by shorting the name with the closed waterway behind it. That is a grind lower, not a capitulation. The honest conclusion is that this name does not offer the violent, price-insensitive flush that makes for a great entry. It offers a scheduled disappointment. Investors should size expectations accordingly: the wash-out to wait for is an information event, not a liquidity event.
moderator_conclusion: This is a good company at a fair price on the wrong day, and the discipline is to say so rather than to reach. Three findings drive the call. First, the cheapness is not real. Price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6 times, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield and €2.93 billion of apparent net cash are the same €3.74 billion of customer advances counted three ways. Management is honest enough to publish the true figure — roughly €1 billion of net cash excluding project-related money — and on that basis the enterprise is worth about €4.8 billion against roughly €600 million of 2026 EBITDA, or about 8 times. Our sum-of-the-parts, valuing the plant-building engine at 6 times and the technology and catalyst arm at 10.5 times and adding the honest cash, lands at €35 against a €33.32 share price. Cross-checked independently against management's own 2028 framework discounted back, it lands in the same place. There is no material margin of safety here. Second, the catalysts are behind us, not ahead. The North Field West award, the record €6.05 billion of first-quarter orders, the 27% backlog build to €20.2 billion, the Ecovyst deal and the dividend have all fired and been reported. The buyback ended on 2026-07-01. What is left is a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — undated, third-party, and moving against us. Third, and decisively, the regime we operate in penalises exactly this shape. Our current market read explicitly warns against theses hinging on one shared macro factor, and directs us to deploy into names orthogonal to oil and to de-risk oil-sensitive exposure mid-event. Technip Energies is the opposite of orthogonal: 82 million tonnes per annum of LNG under construction behind a waterway that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy declared closed on 2026-07-12. Our own regime tripwire for Hormuz re-escalation, marked not-breached on 2026-07-01 when Brent was falling and a truce held, has since breached on dated facts. And the regime favours structural special situations — distressed, spin-offs, forced sellers — of which this is none. So: wait for the wash-out. The thesis is real and the business deserves respect. Management delivered 2024 above plan, delivered 2025 exactly as guided fourteen months earlier, lifted the technology segment's margin from 12.9% to a record 15.3%, bought recurring catalyst revenue at a sensible price, and volunteers the cash number that makes them look worse. That earns a credibility score of 4 and a stable trajectory. But the specific event to wait for is 2026-07-30, thirteen days away, when management must reconcile guidance whose stated precondition has publicly failed against a consensus that still assumes it held. Buying fair value into a probable second guidance cut is not investing, it is hoping. On the value case judged alone — ignoring the catalyst and the regime entirely — this rates a 3 rather than higher for the same arithmetic reason: a quality franchise with rising returns and a genuine narrow moat, but priced at roughly what it is worth once the float is stripped out. It is not a value trap — the moat is narrow rather than eroding, returns are rising, and the company sits on the winning side of decarbonisation with nearly 40% of orders now in that market. It is simply not cheap. Revisit on a second cut, on evidence the deferral is converting rather than evaporating, or on a share price in the mid-twenties, where the honest sum-of-the-parts would finally offer the margin of safety the screen wrongly claims it already offers.
sop_breakdown: Base case, valuing the two operating segments separately and then adding the honest cash. Project Delivery — the long-cycle plant-building engine — on 2026 revenue of €6.0 billion (the midpoint of the guidance cut on 2026-04-30) at a 7.0% EBITDA margin = €420 million, valued at 6.0 times enterprise value to EBITDA = €2.52 billion. This multiple credits some of the peer group's re-rating (Subsea 7 and Saipem sit near 6.5 times) but not all of it, because Technip Energies is the one name in the cohort whose construction sites and module logistics run through a closed waterway. risk_reward: From €33.32, the adverse case breaks to €22 on a prolonged closure with margin leakage and a technology-segment revenue shortfall; the base case is €35 over about 18 months as the strait reopens and the €20.2 billion backlog converts; the favourable case is €44 if the deferred €500-600 million returns in full and the technology segment's record margin holds. catalyst_status: SOFT_EXTENDED — the catalysts that would re-rate this name have either already fired or depend on a third party in a war zone. They are treated as evidence, not as commentary.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management has told across these five calls is remarkably consistent in structure and quietly different in emphasis by the end.

**Where it started (February 2025).** The pitch was growth and scale. Chief executive Arnaud Pieton opened the full-year 2024 call with "our unparalleled value proposition," a backlog "approaching €20 billion," order intake above €10 billion for a second straight year, and a 2028 roadmap of "over €8.6 billion in revenue, over €800 million EBITDA and a free cash flow conversion between 70% to 85%." The dividend was raised nearly 50%. The tone was expansionary: a new venture (Reju, the textile-recycling company) was floated as potentially "a €2 billion revenue company by 2034."

**Where it drifted (mid-2025).** The emphasis moved from winning work to *executing* work. By April 2025 Pieton was explicit: "our foremost priority, a sound and high-quality execution." That is a meaningful shift in a project business — it signals the company has more backlog than it can comfortably digest and that the risk has migrated from the order book to the site. Simultaneously the shorter-cycle Technology, Products and Services segment (the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm, hereafter the technology segment) began missing on revenue, and management "widened the revenue range" for it while keeping the margin promise.

**Where the story rebalanced (late 2025).** A genuine and underappreciated pivot happened here. The technology segment stopped being the growth story and became the *quality* story: revenue fell 9% in 2025 but its EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, as a percentage of revenue) hit a record 14.3%. Management leaned into this, acquiring Ecovyst's Advanced Materials & Catalysts business — closed 2025-12-31 — explicitly because "around 70% of AM&C revenues are tied to operating expenditures, which will improve our long-term revenue visibility." That is a company deliberately buying recurring revenue to offset the lumpiness of its project engine. It is the single most strategically intelligent thing in this transcript set.

**Where it ended (February 2026).** Record revenue of €7.2 billion, record EBITDA of €638 million, a €1.00 dividend (up 18%), a €150 million buyback, and the North Field West award in Qatar announced the day before the call. But buried in the same call was a fact that deserved more attention than it got: project-delivery backlog *fell 18%* year over year to €14.4 billion "with some major awards shifting right." Management's answer was to point forward — "we anticipate an inflection." The inflection did arrive (Q1 2026 order intake of €6.0 billion). The war did too.

**What was quietly dropped:** the green-hydrogen growth leg. In October 2025 Pieton conceded, "where we would have hoped further acceleration, it's in the space of green hydrogen... the business plan is not exactly as we would have expected." That was introduced as a pillar in 2024 and is now a footnote. Reju has also gone from "€2 billion by 2034" to a cost line management defends by explaining it is spending *less* than budgeted.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: High — with one material, recent, and largely exogenous failure.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Selectivity" replaced "growth" as the defining word.** February 2025: "expanding and diversifying our portfolio." February 2026: "controlled quality growth underpinned by our robust selectivity-driven backlog." The company stopped promising more and started promising better. In an engineering-and-construction business, that is usually a sign of a maturing cycle, not of virtue.
- **The capital-allocation language migrated from investing to returning.** The 2024 framework was "dividend growth and strategic technology driven investments." By February 2026 the concrete actions were a dividend and a buyback; the "adjacent business models" venture is now described in terms of how little it costs. Management is signalling, without saying it, that the venture-building phase is over.
- **Catalysts became the strategic centre of gravity.** Pieton in July 2025: "the catalyst in our world is... the main brick and the main precursor to any product development at scale." Three months later they bought a catalyst business. The tell preceded the transaction by a quarter.
- **"Lumpiness is part of our life"** (February 2026) is a new phrase and an important one. It is management pre-framing volatile order intake as structural rather than as a performance signal — reasonable, and also a hedge being laid down in advance.
- **The tone toward the press hardened** in the final call. That is usually a proxy for how much scrutiny the Qatar projects were drawing before the market understood why.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is a well-run, honest, cash-generative engineering franchise whose earnings mix is genuinely improving and whose project engine has been hit by a war it did not cause and cannot fix. The internal machinery is working. The external route is closed.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** the cheapness is not what it appears, and the timing is worse than the market has priced. Price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield and €2.93 billion of "net cash" are all the same customer-advance float counted three ways. On the honest basis management itself publishes — roughly €1 billion of adjusted net cash — the company trades at approximately 8x 2026 EBITDA. That is fair. Meanwhile, management's April guidance cut was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East normalising by the end of the second quarter, and it did not: the truce collapsed on 2026-07-08 and the strait was declared closed on 2026-07-12. Half-year results land on 2026-07-30. Consensus for that print sits at €1.89 billion of revenue — above the disrupted first quarter's €1.78 billion — which means the street is still carrying an assumption that the facts have already killed. Pay fair value for a good business *before* a likely second guidance cut, and you have bought the right company on the wrong day.

**Economic moat: NARROW.** The moat type is intangible — proprietary process technology (ethylene furnaces, the Canopy and Cansolv carbon-capture solutions, the Hummingbird catalyst), reinforced by an exclusive global alliance with Shell and by incumbency-plus-replication on the Qatar North Field trains, where having built NFE and NFS demonstrably won NFW. The evidence supports narrow, not wide: return on invested capital of 11.3% and return on equity of 23.8% are solidly above the cost of capital and rising, but group EBITDA margins are around 8.8% and gross margin is a stable 13.4% — the economics of a disciplined contractor, not of a franchise with pricing power. The asset-light model with negative capital employed is a genuine structural advantage and the reason returns look as good as they do.

**Moat trend: STABLE, with a widening tendency worth watching.** The technology segment's margin has expanded 240 basis points and then 140 basis points in successive periods, return on invested capital is rising, and the catalyst acquisition adds recurring, higher-margin revenue. That is widening. It is offset by the project-delivery margin guide being cut from around 8% to 6.5–7.5%. Net: stable.

**Secular threat: manageable.** This company sits on the *right* side of the energy transition, not the wrong one. Decarbonisation-related work now represents nearly 40% of order intake — carbon capture, blue and green molecules, sustainable fuels, circularity. The liquefied-natural-gas exposure that looks like fossil-fuel risk is, on management's own logic (October 2025), a supply-led, long-cycle market where customers underwrite against 2040 demand and where cheaper gas "would just attract more customers." The real risk here is cyclical and geopolitical, not terminal.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Neither, cleanly — and that is the awkward answer. The base is not shrinking: backlog is €20.2 billion, order intake in the first quarter of 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025, and no contracts were cancelled. But the cheapness is substantially an accounting artefact of customer float rather than a fear-print. Adjust for it and the stock is priced roughly where a good contractor with a live single-country logistics problem ought to be priced. The mispricing to hunt for here is not in the valuation — it is in the calendar.

# Forensic Dossier — Technip Energies N.V. (TE.PA)
**Prepared:** 2026-07-17 · **Listing:** Euronext Paris, euros · **Price used:** €33.32 (live quote, 2026-07-16 close/last)
**Transcripts reviewed:** FY2024 (2025-02-27), Q1 2025 (2025-04-30), H1 2025 (2025-07-31), 9M 2025 (2025-10-30), FY2025 (2026-02-26)
**Note on scope:** the transcript bundle ends at the full-year 2025 call. The two most important events for this name — the Q1 2026 guidance cut on 2026-04-30 and the collapse of the Strait of Hormuz truce in July 2026 — post-date the bundle and were verified independently from live sources. They are treated as evidence, not as commentary.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management has told across these five calls is remarkably consistent in structure and quietly different in emphasis by the end.

**Where it started (February 2025).** The pitch was growth and scale. Chief executive Arnaud Pieton opened the full-year 2024 call with "our unparalleled value proposition," a backlog "approaching €20 billion," order intake above €10 billion for a second straight year, and a 2028 roadmap of "over €8.6 billion in revenue, over €800 million EBITDA and a free cash flow conversion between 70% to 85%." The dividend was raised nearly 50%. The tone was expansionary: a new venture (Reju, the textile-recycling company) was floated as potentially "a €2 billion revenue company by 2034."

**Where it drifted (mid-2025).** The emphasis moved from winning work to *executing* work. By April 2025 Pieton was explicit: "our foremost priority, a sound and high-quality execution." That is a meaningful shift in a project business — it signals the company has more backlog than it can comfortably digest and that the risk has migrated from the order book to the site. Simultaneously the shorter-cycle Technology, Products and Services segment (the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm, hereafter the technology segment) began missing on revenue, and management "widened the revenue range" for it while keeping the margin promise.

**Where the story rebalanced (late 2025).** A genuine and underappreciated pivot happened here. The technology segment stopped being the growth story and became the *quality* story: revenue fell 9% in 2025 but its EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, as a percentage of revenue) hit a record 14.3%. Management leaned into this, acquiring Ecovyst's Advanced Materials & Catalysts business — closed 2025-12-31 — explicitly because "around 70% of AM&C revenues are tied to operating expenditures, which will improve our long-term revenue visibility." That is a company deliberately buying recurring revenue to offset the lumpiness of its project engine. It is the single most strategically intelligent thing in this transcript set.

**Where it ended (February 2026).** Record revenue of €7.2 billion, record EBITDA of €638 million, a €1.00 dividend (up 18%), a €150 million buyback, and the North Field West award in Qatar announced the day before the call. But buried in the same call was a fact that deserved more attention than it got: project-delivery backlog *fell 18%* year over year to €14.4 billion "with some major awards shifting right." Management's answer was to point forward — "we anticipate an inflection." The inflection did arrive (Q1 2026 order intake of €6.0 billion). The war did too.

**What was quietly dropped:** the green-hydrogen growth leg. In October 2025 Pieton conceded, "where we would have hoped further acceleration, it's in the space of green hydrogen... the business plan is not exactly as we would have expected." That was introduced as a pillar in 2024 and is now a footnote. Reju has also gone from "€2 billion by 2034" to a cost line management defends by explaining it is spending *less* than budgeted.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

|---|---|---|---|
| "Our strong net cash balance sheet gives us real payout" | FY2025 | Balance sheet at 2026-03-31: cash €4.17B, total debt €1.25B → apparent net cash €2.93B. But contract liabilities (customer advances) were €3.74B at year-end 2025. Management's own adjusted figure: "net cash adjusted for project-related cash of approximately EUR 1 billion." | **Matches — because management tells the truth on this.** The screener's €2.93B is float, not equity value. Credit management for disclosing the honest number themselves. |
| 2028 roadmap: ">€8.6B revenue, >€800M EBITDA, 70–85% cash conversion" | FY2024 → FY2025 | 2025 actual: €7.2B revenue, €638M EBITDA, 91% conversion. Cash conversion is being *over*-delivered; revenue and EBITDA need roughly 6% and 8% compound growth to land. | **On track, but the 2026 cut consumes a year of the runway.** |

Full-year 2025 free cash flow excluding one-offs: €578M, up 5%. Reported annual free cash flow fell 24.9% year over year. | **Poorer than it looks.** The gap between €897M trailing and €578M underlying is customer advances arriving with the €6.0B of Q1 2026 orders. That is a financing inflow wearing an operating-cash costume, and it reverses as projects complete. |

Q1 2026 earnings per share €0.48 against €0.57 expected. | **Diverges hardest.** The resilience claim was tested by exactly the scenario it was written to cover, and it did not hold. |

**The central forensic finding.** Three of the four things that make this stock screen cheap — price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield, and €2.93 billion of "net cash" — are all inflated by the same item: money customers paid in advance for work not yet done. Strip it out and the enterprise value is roughly €4.8 billion against 2026 EBITDA of about €600 million, or roughly 8x. That is a fair price for a good engineering firm. It is not a bargain. The company is not hiding this; the screen is simply reading the balance sheet the way an industrial company's balance sheet reads, and this is not an industrial company's balance sheet.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining — from expansionary to defensive, in measured steps.**

| Quarter | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| FY2024 (Feb 2025) | "Outstanding 2024 performance"; "I am thrilled with our commercial success"; near-50% dividend increase | Peak offensive. Superlatives, capital returns, new ventures. |
| Q1 2025 | "Given the uncertainty surrounding policies and macroeconomic environment, we have widened the revenue range"; "we just felt it was cautious to widen the range just in case" | First defensive tell. The hedge is pre-emptive and self-aware. |
| H1 2025 | "Our consistent results despite a complex macroeconomic environment" | "Despite" enters the vocabulary. Language shifts from growth to durability. |
| 9M 2025 | "It's a bit of a game of resilience"; "a bit of a disappointment in some of those new markets" | Notably candid. Pieton concedes the green-hydrogen leg is not working. This is the most honest moment in the set. |
| FY2025 (Feb 2026) | "Controlled quality growth"; "let's not believe everything that we can read in the press" (on NFE progress); "lumpiness is part of our life" | Fully defensive framing, plus one flash of irritation at press scrutiny of the Qatar project. |

Guidance became *more* specific over the period, not less — segment-level guidance was introduced at the November 2024 capital markets day and maintained. That is a confidence signal and cuts against the tone read. The honest summary: management got steadily more cautious in language while getting steadily more precise in numbers. That is the profile of a credible team facing a worsening environment, not an evasive one.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: High — with one material, recent, and largely exogenous failure.**

- **2024 delivered above plan.** Revenue "exceeding the top end of our Q3 upgraded guidance range at close to €7 billion." Guidance raised then beaten.
- **2025 guidance, given November 2024, was confirmed at Q1, H1 and 9M and then delivered.** Revenue €7.2B and EBITDA €638M both landed. Project-delivery margin came in "in line with our guidance of around 8%," exactly as promised each quarter. The technology segment's full-year margin guidance was *upgraded* mid-year and delivered at a record 14.3%.
- **A visible sandbagging pattern exists on the technology segment.** Management widened the revenue range downward in April 2025, then beat on margin all year. They guide the number they control (margin) and hedge the number they do not (revenue timing). That is honest, not manipulative — but it means the technology-segment revenue guide carries a deliberate discount.
- **The 2026 guide broke.** On 2026-04-30 project-delivery revenue was cut roughly 8% and its margin cut by around 100 basis points, with €500–600 million of revenue deferred beyond 2026. Chief financial officer Bruno Vibert told reporters no contracts were cancelled and that it was "just a shift" of activity into 2027 and 2028.
- **The reason this matters more than the cut itself:** Pieton's cut was explicitly conditional — "Assuming the situation in the Middle East normalizes by the end of the second quarter, we estimate that around 500-600 million euros in revenue will be deferred beyond 2026." That precondition failed. The interim US-Iran truce broke down on 2026-07-08 when Iran struck commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz; on 2026-07-12 the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy declared the strait closed, with transits running at roughly 10 per day against a pre-crisis baseline of 88.

The earnings-beat rate of 3 of 6 quarters (50%) in the screener understates this team. They beat consistently on the metrics they guide and miss on quarterly consensus estimates that they never endorsed. The Q1 2026 miss (€0.48 against €0.57) is the exception that is genuinely informative.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The technology segment's backlog coverage — asked three times, never fully answered.** Paul Redman (BNP Paribas Exane) in February 2026: "what gives you the confidence to guide to EUR 2 billion to EUR 2.2 billion of revenue in '26... it looks like you've only got EUR 1 billion in the backlog at the moment." Vibert's answer relied on three items that are *not* in backlog: the acquired catalyst business, consultancy work booked and burned, and awards with "a clear line of sight." That is three layers of un-contracted revenue supporting a third of group turnover. This is the segment carrying the margin story, and its revenue is the least visible thing in the company.
- **Qatar project progress — met with defensiveness.** Jamie Franklin (Jefferies) and others pressed on NFE timing. Pieton's February 2026 answer — "let's not believe everything that we can read in the press... If the client was unhappy, I think we would have heard about it and probably we would not have been awarded NFW" — is an argument from the client's revealed preference, not from the schedule. It is a reasonable argument. It is also not an answer to the question asked, and the questioner had identified the right risk area roughly two months before a war shut the logistics route to that exact site.
- **Project contingencies — deliberately opaque.** Bertrand Hodee (Kepler Cheuvreux) reverse-engineered a roughly €250 million increase in project contingencies in H1 2025. Vibert's reply: "maybe I won't go into the full details. Otherwise, we will both lose everyone on the call," then a four-factor explanation that confirmed nothing. Contingency levels are the single most important undisclosed number in an engineering-and-construction company, because they determine how much of the backlog margin is real. The analyst was right to push; he did not get it.
- **The gap analysts have not priced.** Nobody in these calls asked what happens to cash flow when the Qatar projects finish. Customer advances fund this balance sheet. NFE's first train is due on stream around mid-2026 and North Field West "won't have a major contribution this year." The advance-payment cycle turning is a mechanical, foreseeable drag, and it is absent from the discussion.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **Earnings per share have gone backwards** — €2.17 (2024) → €2.04 (2025), and only 4% growth excluding one-offs, against a 2028 plan that needs high-single-digit compounding.

🔴 **Project-delivery backlog fell 18% in 2025** to €14.4 billion, disclosed at the full-year call with the softening phrase "some major awards shifting right." Management's forward-pointing was vindicated in Q1 2026, but the disclosure lagged the deterioration by three quarters.

🔴 **The resilience claim failed its first real test.** "TEN will remain strong in any scenario" (Q1 2025) preceded a two-part guidance cut a year later driven by exactly the geopolitical scenario in question. Concentration in the Middle East is the un-hedged exposure the equity story does not price.

🔴 **Contingency disclosure is deliberately withheld** (H1 2025, Vibert). In a business where backlog margin is an estimate, this is the number that would let an outsider check the estimate.

🔴 **The green-hydrogen leg quietly failed** (9M 2025) after being sold as a growth pillar.

🟢 **Management discloses the honest cash number.** They publish "net cash adjusted for project-associated cash" — roughly €1 billion — rather than letting the €2.9 billion gross figure stand. Very few managements volunteer the number that makes them look worse.

🟢 **The technology-segment margin trajectory is real and rising** — 12.9% → 14.3% → 15.3% in Q1 2026, corroborated by return on invested capital moving 10.5% → 11.3%.

🟢 **The Ecovyst catalyst acquisition is strategically correct and cheap in risk terms** — recurring, operating-expenditure-linked revenue at roughly 25% EBITDA margins, bought without impairing the investment-grade rating.

🟢 **The Shell alliance on post-combustion carbon capture** (H1 2025) is an exclusive global arrangement — the closest thing here to a durable competitive advantage.

🟢 **Guidance discipline is genuine** — 2025 segment guidance was set 14 months ahead, confirmed four times, and delivered.

🟢 **No contracts cancelled** through the disruption (Vibert, April 2026). The damage is timing, not demand.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Selectivity" replaced "growth" as the defining word.** February 2025: "expanding and diversifying our portfolio." February 2026: "controlled quality growth underpinned by our robust selectivity-driven backlog." The company stopped promising more and started promising better. In an engineering-and-construction business, that is usually a sign of a maturing cycle, not of virtue.
- **The capital-allocation language migrated from investing to returning.** The 2024 framework was "dividend growth and strategic technology driven investments." By February 2026 the concrete actions were a dividend and a buyback; the "adjacent business models" venture is now described in terms of how little it costs. Management is signalling, without saying it, that the venture-building phase is over.
- **Catalysts became the strategic centre of gravity.** Pieton in July 2025: "the catalyst in our world is... the main brick and the main precursor to any product development at scale." Three months later they bought a catalyst business. The tell preceded the transaction by a quarter.
- **"Lumpiness is part of our life"** (February 2026) is a new phrase and an important one. It is management pre-framing volatile order intake as structural rather than as a performance signal — reasonable, and also a hedge being laid down in advance.
- **The tone toward the press hardened** in the final call. That is usually a proxy for how much scrutiny the Qatar projects were drawing before the market understood why.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is a well-run, honest, cash-generative engineering franchise whose earnings mix is genuinely improving and whose project engine has been hit by a war it did not cause and cannot fix. The internal machinery is working. The external route is closed.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** the cheapness is not what it appears, and the timing is worse than the market has priced. Price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield and €2.93 billion of "net cash" are all the same customer-advance float counted three ways. On the honest basis management itself publishes — roughly €1 billion of adjusted net cash — the company trades at approximately 8x 2026 EBITDA. That is fair. Meanwhile, management's April guidance cut was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East normalising by the end of the second quarter, and it did not: the truce collapsed on 2026-07-08 and the strait was declared closed on 2026-07-12. Half-year results land on 2026-07-30. Consensus for that print sits at €1.89 billion of revenue — above the disrupted first quarter's €1.78 billion — which means the street is still carrying an assumption that the facts have already killed. Pay fair value for a good business *before* a likely second guidance cut, and you have bought the right company on the wrong day.

**Economic moat: NARROW.** The moat type is intangible — proprietary process technology (ethylene furnaces, the Canopy and Cansolv carbon-capture solutions, the Hummingbird catalyst), reinforced by an exclusive global alliance with Shell and by incumbency-plus-replication on the Qatar North Field trains, where having built NFE and NFS demonstrably won NFW. The evidence supports narrow, not wide: return on invested capital of 11.3% and return on equity of 23.8% are solidly above the cost of capital and rising, but group EBITDA margins are around 8.8% and gross margin is a stable 13.4% — the economics of a disciplined contractor, not of a franchise with pricing power. The asset-light model with negative capital employed is a genuine structural advantage and the reason returns look as good as they do.

**Moat trend: STABLE, with a widening tendency worth watching.** The technology segment's margin has expanded 240 basis points and then 140 basis points in successive periods, return on invested capital is rising, and the catalyst acquisition adds recurring, higher-margin revenue. That is widening. It is offset by the project-delivery margin guide being cut from around 8% to 6.5–7.5%. Net: stable.

**Secular threat: manageable.** This company sits on the *right* side of the energy transition, not the wrong one. Decarbonisation-related work now represents nearly 40% of order intake — carbon capture, blue and green molecules, sustainable fuels, circularity. The liquefied-natural-gas exposure that looks like fossil-fuel risk is, on management's own logic (October 2025), a supply-led, long-cycle market where customers underwrite against 2040 demand and where cheaper gas "would just attract more customers." The real risk here is cyclical and geopolitical, not terminal.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Neither, cleanly — and that is the awkward answer. The base is not shrinking: backlog is €20.2 billion, order intake in the first quarter of 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025, and no contracts were cancelled. But the cheapness is substantially an accounting artefact of customer float rather than a fear-print. Adjust for it and the stock is priced roughly where a good contractor with a live single-country logistics problem ought to be priced. The mispricing to hunt for here is not in the valuation — it is in the calendar.

# Forensic Dossier — Technip Energies N.V. (TE.PA)
**Prepared:** 2026-07-17 · **Listing:** Euronext Paris, euros · **Price used:** €33.32 (live quote, 2026-07-16 close/last)

They are treated as evidence, not as commentary.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management has told across these five calls is remarkably consistent in structure and quietly different in emphasis by the end.

**Where it started (February 2025).** The pitch was growth and scale. Chief executive Arnaud Pieton opened the full-year 2024 call with "our unparalleled value proposition," a backlog "approaching €20 billion," order intake above €10 billion for a second straight year, and a 2028 roadmap of "over €8.6 billion in revenue, over €800 million EBITDA and a free cash flow conversion between 70% to 85%." The dividend was raised nearly 50%. The tone was expansionary: a new venture (Reju, the textile-recycling company) was floated as potentially "a €2 billion revenue company by 2034."

**Where it drifted (mid-2025).** The emphasis moved from winning work to *executing* work. By April 2025 Pieton was explicit: "our foremost priority, a sound and high-quality execution." That is a meaningful shift in a project business — it signals the company has more backlog than it can comfortably digest and that the risk has migrated from the order book to the site. Simultaneously the shorter-cycle Technology, Products and Services segment (the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm, hereafter the technology segment) began missing on revenue, and management "widened the revenue range" for it while keeping the margin promise.

**Where the story rebalanced (late 2025).** A genuine and underappreciated pivot happened here. The technology segment stopped being the growth story and became the *quality* story: revenue fell 9% in 2025 but its EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, as a percentage of revenue) hit a record 14.3%. Management leaned into this, acquiring Ecovyst's Advanced Materials & Catalysts business — closed 2025-12-31 — explicitly because "around 70% of AM&C revenues are tied to operating expenditures, which will improve our long-term revenue visibility." That is a company deliberately buying recurring revenue to offset the lumpiness of its project engine. It is the single most strategically intelligent thing in this transcript set.

**Where it ended (February 2026).** Record revenue of €7.2 billion, record EBITDA of €638 million, a €1.00 dividend (up 18%), a €150 million buyback, and the North Field West award in Qatar announced the day before the call. But buried in the same call was a fact that deserved more attention than it got: project-delivery backlog *fell 18%* year over year to €14.4 billion "with some major awards shifting right." Management's answer was to point forward — "we anticipate an inflection." The inflection did arrive (Q1 2026 order intake of €6.0 billion). The war did too.

**What was quietly dropped:** the green-hydrogen growth leg. In October 2025 Pieton conceded, "where we would have hoped further acceleration, it's in the space of green hydrogen... the business plan is not exactly as we would have expected." That was introduced as a pillar in 2024 and is now a footnote. Reju has also gone from "€2 billion by 2034" to a cost line management defends by explaining it is spending *less* than budgeted.

**Economic moat: NARROW.** The moat type is intangible — proprietary process technology (ethylene furnaces, the Canopy and Cansolv carbon-capture solutions, the Hummingbird catalyst), reinforced by an exclusive global alliance with Shell and by incumbency-plus-replication on the Qatar North Field trains, where having built NFE and NFS demonstrably won NFW. **Moat trend: STABLE, with a widening tendency worth watching.** The technology segment's margin has expanded 240 basis points and then 140 basis points in successive periods, return on invested capital is rising, and the catalyst acquisition adds recurring, higher-margin revenue. That is widening. It is offset by the project-delivery margin guide being cut from around 8% to 6.5–7.5%. Net: stable.

**Secular threat: manageable.** This company sits on the *right* side of the energy transition, not the wrong one. Decarbonisation-related work now represents nearly 40% of order intake — carbon capture, blue and green molecules, sustainable fuels, circularity. The liquefied-natural-gas exposure that looks like fossil-fuel risk is, on management's own logic (October 2025), a supply-led, long-cycle market where customers underwrite against 2040 demand and where cheaper gas "would just attract more customers." The real risk here is cyclical and geopolitical, not terminal.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Neither, cleanly — and that is the awkward answer. The base is not shrinking: backlog is €20.2 billion, order intake in the first quarter of 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025, and no contracts were cancelled. But the cheapness is substantially an accounting artefact of customer float rather than a fear-print. Adjust for it and the stock is priced roughly where a good contractor with a live single-country logistics problem ought to be priced. ## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management has told across these five calls is remarkably consistent in structure and quietly different in emphasis by the end.

**Where it started (February 2025).** The pitch was growth and scale. Chief executive Arnaud Pieton opened the full-year 2024 call with "our unparalleled value proposition," a backlog "approaching €20 billion," order intake above €10 billion for a second straight year, and a 2028 roadmap of "over €8.6 billion in revenue, over €800 million EBITDA and a free cash flow conversion between 70% to 85%." **Where it drifted (mid-2025).** The emphasis moved from winning work to *executing* work. By April 2025 Pieton was explicit: "our foremost priority, a sound and high-quality execution." That is a meaningful shift in a project business — it signals the company has more backlog than it can comfortably digest and that the risk has migrated from the order book to the site. Simultaneously the shorter-cycle Technology, Products and Services segment (the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm, hereafter the technology segment) began missing on revenue, and management "widened the revenue range" for it while keeping the margin promise.

Management leaned into this, acquiring Ecovyst's Advanced Materials & Catalysts business — closed 2025-12-31 — explicitly because "around 70% of AM&C revenues are tied to operating expenditures, which will improve our long-term revenue visibility." Management's answer was to point forward — "we anticipate an inflection." The inflection did arrive (Q1 2026 order intake of €6.0 billion). The war did too.

**What was quietly dropped:** the green-hydrogen growth leg. In October 2025 Pieton conceded, "where we would have hoped further acceleration, it's in the space of green hydrogen... the business plan is not exactly as we would have expected." That was introduced as a pillar in 2024 and is now a footnote. Reju has also gone from "€2 billion by 2034" to a cost line management defends by explaining it is spending *less* than budgeted.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: High — with one material, recent, and largely exogenous failure.**

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Selectivity" replaced "growth" as the defining word.** February 2025: "expanding and diversifying our portfolio." February 2026: "controlled quality growth underpinned by our robust selectivity-driven backlog." The company stopped promising more and started promising better. In an engineering-and-construction business, that is usually a sign of a maturing cycle, not of virtue.
- **The capital-allocation language migrated from investing to returning.** The 2024 framework was "dividend growth and strategic technology driven investments." By February 2026 the concrete actions were a dividend and a buyback; the "adjacent business models" venture is now described in terms of how little it costs. Management is signalling, without saying it, that the venture-building phase is over.
- **Catalysts became the strategic centre of gravity.** Pieton in July 2025: "the catalyst in our world is... the main brick and the main precursor to any product development at scale." Three months later they bought a catalyst business. The tell preceded the transaction by a quarter.
- **"Lumpiness is part of our life"** (February 2026) is a new phrase and an important one. It is management pre-framing volatile order intake as structural rather than as a performance signal — reasonable, and also a hedge being laid down in advance.
- **The tone toward the press hardened** in the final call. That is usually a proxy for how much scrutiny the Qatar projects were drawing before the market understood why.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is a well-run, honest, cash-generative engineering franchise whose earnings mix is genuinely improving and whose project engine has been hit by a war it did not cause and cannot fix. The internal machinery is working. The external route is closed.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** the cheapness is not what it appears, and the timing is worse than the market has priced. Price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield and €2.93 billion of "net cash" are all the same customer-advance float counted three ways. On the honest basis management itself publishes — roughly €1 billion of adjusted net cash — the company trades at approximately 8x 2026 EBITDA. That is fair. Meanwhile, management's April guidance cut was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East normalising by the end of the second quarter, and it did not: the truce collapsed on 2026-07-08 and the strait was declared closed on 2026-07-12. Half-year results land on 2026-07-30. Consensus for that print sits at €1.89 billion of revenue — above the disrupted first quarter's €1.78 billion — which means the street is still carrying an assumption that the facts have already killed. Pay fair value for a good business *before* a likely second guidance cut, and you have bought the right company on the wrong day.

**Economic moat: NARROW.** The moat type is intangible — proprietary process technology (ethylene furnaces, the Canopy and Cansolv carbon-capture solutions, the Hummingbird catalyst), reinforced by an exclusive global alliance with Shell and by incumbency-plus-replication on the Qatar North Field trains, where having built NFE and NFS demonstrably won NFW. The evidence supports narrow, not wide: return on invested capital of 11.3% and return on equity of 23.8% are solidly above the cost of capital and rising, but group EBITDA margins are around 8.8% and gross margin is a stable 13.4% — the economics of a disciplined contractor, not of a franchise with pricing power. The asset-light model with negative capital employed is a genuine structural advantage and the reason returns look as good as they do.

**Moat trend: STABLE, with a widening tendency worth watching.** The technology segment's margin has expanded 240 basis points and then 140 basis points in successive periods, return on invested capital is rising, and the catalyst acquisition adds recurring, higher-margin revenue. That is widening. It is offset by the project-delivery margin guide being cut from around 8% to 6.5–7.5%. Net: stable.

**Secular threat: manageable.** This company sits on the *right* side of the energy transition, not the wrong one. Decarbonisation-related work now represents nearly 40% of order intake — carbon capture, blue and green molecules, sustainable fuels, circularity. The liquefied-natural-gas exposure that looks like fossil-fuel risk is, on management's own logic (October 2025), a supply-led, long-cycle market where customers underwrite against 2040 demand and where cheaper gas "would just attract more customers." The real risk here is cyclical and geopolitical, not terminal.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Neither, cleanly — and that is the awkward answer. The base is not shrinking: backlog is €20.2 billion, order intake in the first quarter of 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025, and no contracts were cancelled. But the cheapness is substantially an accounting artefact of customer float rather than a fear-print. Adjust for it and the stock is priced roughly where a good contractor with a live single-country logistics problem ought to be priced. The mispricing to hunt for here is not in the valuation — it is in the calendar.

# Forensic Dossier — Technip Energies N.V. (TE.PA)
**Prepared:** 2026-07-17 · **Listing:** Euronext Paris, euros · **Price used:** €33.32 (live quote, 2026-07-16 close/last)
**Transcripts reviewed:** FY2024 (2025-02-27), Q1 2025 (2025-04-30), H1 2025 (2025-07-31), 9M 2025 (2025-10-30), FY2025 (2026-02-26)
**Note on scope:** the transcript bundle ends at the full-year 2025 call. The two most important events for this name — the Q1 2026 guidance cut on 2026-04-30 and the collapse of the Strait of Hormuz truce in July 2026 — post-date the bundle and were verified independently from live sources. They are treated as evidence, not as commentary.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management has told across these five calls is remarkably consistent in structure and quietly different in emphasis by the end.

**Where it started (February 2025).** The pitch was growth and scale. Chief executive Arnaud Pieton opened the full-year 2024 call with "our unparalleled value proposition," a backlog "approaching €20 billion," order intake above €10 billion for a second straight year, and a 2028 roadmap of "over €8.6 billion in revenue, over €800 million EBITDA and a free cash flow conversion between 70% to 85%." The dividend was raised nearly 50%. The tone was expansionary: a new venture (Reju, the textile-recycling company) was floated as potentially "a €2 billion revenue company by 2034."

**Where it drifted (mid-2025).** The emphasis moved from winning work to *executing* work. By April 2025 Pieton was explicit: "our foremost priority, a sound and high-quality execution." That is a meaningful shift in a project business — it signals the company has more backlog than it can comfortably digest and that the risk has migrated from the order book to the site. Simultaneously the shorter-cycle Technology, Products and Services segment (the higher-margin technology, equipment and consultancy arm, hereafter the technology segment) began missing on revenue, and management "widened the revenue range" for it while keeping the margin promise.

**Where the story rebalanced (late 2025).** A genuine and underappreciated pivot happened here. The technology segment stopped being the growth story and became the *quality* story: revenue fell 9% in 2025 but its EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, as a percentage of revenue) hit a record 14.3%. Management leaned into this, acquiring Ecovyst's Advanced Materials & Catalysts business — closed 2025-12-31 — explicitly because "around 70% of AM&C revenues are tied to operating expenditures, which will improve our long-term revenue visibility." That is a company deliberately buying recurring revenue to offset the lumpiness of its project engine. It is the single most strategically intelligent thing in this transcript set.

**Where it ended (February 2026).** Record revenue of €7.2 billion, record EBITDA of €638 million, a €1.00 dividend (up 18%), a €150 million buyback, and the North Field West award in Qatar announced the day before the call. But buried in the same call was a fact that deserved more attention than it got: project-delivery backlog *fell 18%* year over year to €14.4 billion "with some major awards shifting right." Management's answer was to point forward — "we anticipate an inflection." The inflection did arrive (Q1 2026 order intake of €6.0 billion). The war did too.

**What was quietly dropped:** the green-hydrogen growth leg. In October 2025 Pieton conceded, "where we would have hoped further acceleration, it's in the space of green hydrogen... the business plan is not exactly as we would have expected." That was introduced as a pillar in 2024 and is now a footnote. Reju has also gone from "€2 billion by 2034" to a cost line management defends by explaining it is spending *less* than budgeted.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| "Our strong net cash balance sheet gives us real payout" | FY2025 | Balance sheet at 2026-03-31: cash €4.17B, total debt €1.25B → apparent net cash €2.93B. But contract liabilities (customer advances) were €3.74B at year-end 2025. Management's own adjusted figure: "net cash adjusted for project-related cash of approximately EUR 1 billion." | **Matches — because management tells the truth on this.** The screener's €2.93B is float, not equity value. Credit management for disclosing the honest number themselves. |
| 2028 roadmap: ">€8.6B revenue, >€800M EBITDA, 70–85% cash conversion" | FY2024 → FY2025 | 2025 actual: €7.2B revenue, €638M EBITDA, 91% conversion. Cash conversion is being *over*-delivered; revenue and EBITDA need roughly 6% and 8% compound growth to land. | **On track, but the 2026 cut consumes a year of the runway.** |

Full-year 2025 free cash flow excluding one-offs: €578M, up 5%. Q1 2026 earnings per share €0.48 against €0.57 expected. | **Diverges hardest.** The resilience claim was tested by exactly the scenario it was written to cover, and it did not hold. |

**The central forensic finding.** Three of the four things that make this stock screen cheap — price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield, and €2.93 billion of "net cash" — are all inflated by the same item: money customers paid in advance for work not yet done. Strip it out and the enterprise value is roughly €4.8 billion against 2026 EBITDA of about €600 million, or roughly 8x. That is a fair price for a good engineering firm. It is not a bargain. The company is not hiding this; the screen is simply reading the balance sheet the way an industrial company's balance sheet reads, and this is not an industrial company's balance sheet.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining — from expansionary to defensive, in measured steps.**

| Quarter | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| FY2024 (Feb 2025) | "Outstanding 2024 performance"; "I am thrilled with our commercial success"; near-50% dividend increase | Peak offensive. Superlatives, capital returns, new ventures. |
| Q1 2025 | "Given the uncertainty surrounding policies and macroeconomic environment, we have widened the revenue range"; "we just felt it was cautious to widen the range just in case" | First defensive tell. The hedge is pre-emptive and self-aware. |
| H1 2025 | "Our consistent results despite a complex macroeconomic environment" | "Despite" enters the vocabulary. Language shifts from growth to durability. |
| 9M 2025 | "It's a bit of a game of resilience"; "a bit of a disappointment in some of those new markets" | Notably candid. Pieton concedes the green-hydrogen leg is not working. This is the most honest moment in the set. |
| FY2025 (Feb 2026) | "Controlled quality growth"; "let's not believe everything that we can read in the press" (on NFE progress); "lumpiness is part of our life" | Fully defensive framing, plus one flash of irritation at press scrutiny of the Qatar project. |

Guidance became *more* specific over the period, not less — segment-level guidance was introduced at the November 2024 capital markets day and maintained. That is a confidence signal and cuts against the tone read. The honest summary: management got steadily more cautious in language while getting steadily more precise in numbers. That is the profile of a credible team facing a worsening environment, not an evasive one.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: High — with one material, recent, and largely exogenous failure.**

- **2024 delivered above plan.** Revenue "exceeding the top end of our Q3 upgraded guidance range at close to €7 billion." Guidance raised then beaten.
- **2025 guidance, given November 2024, was confirmed at Q1, H1 and 9M and then delivered.** Revenue €7.2B and EBITDA €638M both landed. Project-delivery margin came in "in line with our guidance of around 8%," exactly as promised each quarter. The technology segment's full-year margin guidance was *upgraded* mid-year and delivered at a record 14.3%.
- **A visible sandbagging pattern exists on the technology segment.** Management widened the revenue range downward in April 2025, then beat on margin all year. They guide the number they control (margin) and hedge the number they do not (revenue timing). That is honest, not manipulative — but it means the technology-segment revenue guide carries a deliberate discount.
- **The 2026 guide broke.** On 2026-04-30 project-delivery revenue was cut roughly 8% and its margin cut by around 100 basis points, with €500–600 million of revenue deferred beyond 2026. Chief financial officer Bruno Vibert told reporters no contracts were cancelled and that it was "just a shift" of activity into 2027 and 2028.
- **The reason this matters more than the cut itself:** Pieton's cut was explicitly conditional — "Assuming the situation in the Middle East normalizes by the end of the second quarter, we estimate that around 500-600 million euros in revenue will be deferred beyond 2026." That precondition failed. The interim US-Iran truce broke down on 2026-07-08 when Iran struck commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz; on 2026-07-12 the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy declared the strait closed, with transits running at roughly 10 per day against a pre-crisis baseline of 88.

The earnings-beat rate of 3 of 6 quarters (50%) in the screener understates this team. They beat consistently on the metrics they guide and miss on quarterly consensus estimates that they never endorsed. The Q1 2026 miss (€0.48 against €0.57) is the exception that is genuinely informative.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The technology segment's backlog coverage — asked three times, never fully answered.** Paul Redman (BNP Paribas Exane) in February 2026: "what gives you the confidence to guide to EUR 2 billion to EUR 2.2 billion of revenue in '26... it looks like you've only got EUR 1 billion in the backlog at the moment." Vibert's answer relied on three items that are *not* in backlog: the acquired catalyst business, consultancy work booked and burned, and awards with "a clear line of sight." That is three layers of un-contracted revenue supporting a third of group turnover. This is the segment carrying the margin story, and its revenue is the least visible thing in the company.
- **Qatar project progress — met with defensiveness.** Jamie Franklin (Jefferies) and others pressed on NFE timing. Pieton's February 2026 answer — "let's not believe everything that we can read in the press... If the client was unhappy, I think we would have heard about it and probably we would not have been awarded NFW" — is an argument from the client's revealed preference, not from the schedule. It is a reasonable argument. It is also not an answer to the question asked, and the questioner had identified the right risk area roughly two months before a war shut the logistics route to that exact site.
- **Project contingencies — deliberately opaque.** Bertrand Hodee (Kepler Cheuvreux) reverse-engineered a roughly €250 million increase in project contingencies in H1 2025. Vibert's reply: "maybe I won't go into the full details. Otherwise, we will both lose everyone on the call," then a four-factor explanation that confirmed nothing. Contingency levels are the single most important undisclosed number in an engineering-and-construction company, because they determine how much of the backlog margin is real. The analyst was right to push; he did not get it.
- **The gap analysts have not priced.** Nobody in these calls asked what happens to cash flow when the Qatar projects finish. Customer advances fund this balance sheet. NFE's first train is due on stream around mid-2026 and North Field West "won't have a major contribution this year." The advance-payment cycle turning is a mechanical, foreseeable drag, and it is absent from the discussion.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **Earnings per share have gone backwards** — €2.17 (2024) → €2.04 (2025), and only 4% growth excluding one-offs, against a 2028 plan that needs high-single-digit compounding.

🔴 **Project-delivery backlog fell 18% in 2025** to €14.4 billion, disclosed at the full-year call with the softening phrase "some major awards shifting right." Management's forward-pointing was vindicated in Q1 2026, but the disclosure lagged the deterioration by three quarters.

🔴 **The resilience claim failed its first real test.** "TEN will remain strong in any scenario" (Q1 2025) preceded a two-part guidance cut a year later driven by exactly the geopolitical scenario in question. Concentration in the Middle East is the un-hedged exposure the equity story does not price.

🔴 **Contingency disclosure is deliberately withheld** (H1 2025, Vibert). In a business where backlog margin is an estimate, this is the number that would let an outsider check the estimate.

🔴 **The green-hydrogen leg quietly failed** (9M 2025) after being sold as a growth pillar.

🟢 **Management discloses the honest cash number.** They publish "net cash adjusted for project-associated cash" — roughly €1 billion — rather than letting the €2.9 billion gross figure stand. Very few managements volunteer the number that makes them look worse.

🟢 **The technology-segment margin trajectory is real and rising** — 12.9% → 14.3% → 15.3% in Q1 2026, corroborated by return on invested capital moving 10.5% → 11.3%.

🟢 **The Ecovyst catalyst acquisition is strategically correct and cheap in risk terms** — recurring, operating-expenditure-linked revenue at roughly 25% EBITDA margins, bought without impairing the investment-grade rating.

🟢 **The Shell alliance on post-combustion carbon capture** (H1 2025) is an exclusive global arrangement — the closest thing here to a durable competitive advantage.

🟢 **Guidance discipline is genuine** — 2025 segment guidance was set 14 months ahead, confirmed four times, and delivered.

🟢 **No contracts cancelled** through the disruption (Vibert, April 2026). The damage is timing, not demand.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Selectivity" replaced "growth" as the defining word.** February 2025: "expanding and diversifying our portfolio." February 2026: "controlled quality growth underpinned by our robust selectivity-driven backlog." The company stopped promising more and started promising better. In an engineering-and-construction business, that is usually a sign of a maturing cycle, not of virtue.
- **The capital-allocation language migrated from investing to returning.** The 2024 framework was "dividend growth and strategic technology driven investments." By February 2026 the concrete actions were a dividend and a buyback; the "adjacent business models" venture is now described in terms of how little it costs. Management is signalling, without saying it, that the venture-building phase is over.
- **Catalysts became the strategic centre of gravity.** Pieton in July 2025: "the catalyst in our world is... the main brick and the main precursor to any product development at scale." Three months later they bought a catalyst business. The tell preceded the transaction by a quarter.
- **"Lumpiness is part of our life"** (February 2026) is a new phrase and an important one. It is management pre-framing volatile order intake as structural rather than as a performance signal — reasonable, and also a hedge being laid down in advance.
- **The tone toward the press hardened** in the final call. That is usually a proxy for how much scrutiny the Qatar projects were drawing before the market understood why.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is a well-run, honest, cash-generative engineering franchise whose earnings mix is genuinely improving and whose project engine has been hit by a war it did not cause and cannot fix. The internal machinery is working. The external route is closed.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** the cheapness is not what it appears, and the timing is worse than the market has priced. Price-to-free-cash-flow of 9.6x, a 15.5% free-cash-flow yield and €2.93 billion of "net cash" are all the same customer-advance float counted three ways. On the honest basis management itself publishes — roughly €1 billion of adjusted net cash — the company trades at approximately 8x 2026 EBITDA. That is fair. Meanwhile, management's April guidance cut was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East normalising by the end of the second quarter, and it did not: the truce collapsed on 2026-07-08 and the strait was declared closed on 2026-07-12. Half-year results land on 2026-07-30. Consensus for that print sits at €1.89 billion of revenue — above the disrupted first quarter's €1.78 billion — which means the street is still carrying an assumption that the facts have already killed. Pay fair value for a good business *before* a likely second guidance cut, and you have bought the right company on the wrong day.

**Economic moat: NARROW.** The moat type is intangible — proprietary process technology (ethylene furnaces, the Canopy and Cansolv carbon-capture solutions, the Hummingbird catalyst), reinforced by an exclusive global alliance with Shell and by incumbency-plus-replication on the Qatar North Field trains, where having built NFE and NFS demonstrably won NFW. The evidence supports narrow, not wide: return on invested capital of 11.3% and return on equity of 23.8% are solidly above the cost of capital and rising, but group EBITDA margins are around 8.8% and gross margin is a stable 13.4% — the economics of a disciplined contractor, not of a franchise with pricing power. The asset-light model with negative capital employed is a genuine structural advantage and the reason returns look as good as they do.

**Moat trend: STABLE, with a widening tendency worth watching.** The technology segment's margin has expanded 240 basis points and then 140 basis points in successive periods, return on invested capital is rising, and the catalyst acquisition adds recurring, higher-margin revenue. That is widening. It is offset by the project-delivery margin guide being cut from around 8% to 6.5–7.5%. Net: stable.

**Secular threat: manageable.** This company sits on the *right* side of the energy transition, not the wrong one. Decarbonisation-related work now represents nearly 40% of order intake — carbon capture, blue and green molecules, sustainable fuels, circularity. The liquefied-natural-gas exposure that looks like fossil-fuel risk is, on management's own logic (October 2025), a supply-led, long-cycle market where customers underwrite against 2040 demand and where cheaper gas "would just attract more customers." The real risk here is cyclical and geopolitical, not terminal.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Neither, cleanly — and that is the awkward answer. The base is not shrinking: backlog is €20.2 billion, order intake in the first quarter of 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025, and no contracts were cancelled. But the cheapness is substantially an accounting artefact of customer float rather than a fear-print. Adjust for it and the stock is priced roughly where a good contractor with a live single-country logistics problem ought to be priced. The mispricing to hunt for here is not in the valuation — it is in the calendar.
